questions.question: The tangent at any point of a circle is always perpendicular to which geometric line through the point of contact?
options: The radius through the point of contact
The chord passing through the point
The line segment connecting to the opposite circumference
Any secant line drawn to the circle
questions.explanation: According to Theorem 10.1 in NCERT Mathematics, the tangent at any point of a circle is strictly perpendicular to the radius drawn through the point of contact. Proof: Let line l be the tangent touching the circle at point P with center O. Take any other point Q on line l distinct from P. Because l is a tangent, Q must lie outside the circle. Therefore, distance OQ is strictly greater than the radius OP (OQ > OP). Since this holds for every point on l other than P, OP is the shortest distance from center O to line l, proving OP is perpendicular to l.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 10, Theorem 10.1

questions.question: From an external point P, two tangents PA and PB are drawn to a circle. What is the relation between the lengths of PA and PB?
questions.explanation: Theorem 10.2 of CBSE Class 10 states: The lengths of the two tangents drawn from a single external point to a circle are equal (PA = PB). Proof: Let PA and PB be tangents drawn from point P to a circle with center O, touching at points A and B. Join OA, OB, and OP. In right-angled triangles OPA and OPB: angle OAP = angle OBP = 90 degrees (Theorem 10.1); hypotenuse OP is common (OP = OP); and radius OA = OB. By the RHS congruence criterion, triangle OPA is congruent to triangle OPB, which immediately implies that PA = PB by CPCT.

questions.question: A tangent PQ at a point P of a circle of radius 5 cm meets a line through the centre O at a point Q so that OQ = 12 cm. What is the length of PQ?
questions.explanation: Let O be the center of the circle of radius OP = 5 cm, and PQ be the tangent touching at point P. By Theorem 10.1, the radius OP is perpendicular to the tangent PQ at the point of contact, making triangle OPQ a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse OQ = 12 cm. Applying the Pythagorean theorem: OQ^2 = OP^2 + PQ^2 => 12^2 = 5^2 + PQ^2 => 144 = 25 + PQ^2 => PQ^2 = 144 - 25 = 119. Taking the positive square root gives the tangent length PQ = sqrt(119) cm (approximately 10.91 cm), which cannot be further simplified.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 10, Exercise 10.1 Question 3

questions.subtopic: Tangent Length with Standard Pythagorean Triplet
questions.question: From a point Q, the length of the tangent to a circle is 24 cm and the distance of Q from the centre is 25 cm. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.explanation: In a circle with center O and radius r, let Q be an external point and QP be the tangent touching at point P. By Theorem 10.1, radius OP is perpendicular to tangent QP, forming a right-angled triangle OPQ where hypotenuse OQ = 25 cm and tangent leg PQ = 24 cm. Applying the Pythagorean theorem: OQ^2 = OP^2 + PQ^2 => 25^2 = r^2 + 24^2 => 625 = r^2 + 576 => r^2 = 625 - 576 = 49. Taking the square root yields radius r = sqrt(49) = 7 cm, demonstrating the Pythagorean triplet (7, 24, 25).

questions.subtopic: Supplementary Angles Between Tangents and Centre
questions.question: If TP and TQ are the two tangents to a circle with centre O so that angle POQ = 110 degrees, then what is angle PTQ?
questions.explanation: In quadrilateral OPTQ, TP and TQ are tangents touching the circle at P and Q from external point T. By Theorem 10.1, the tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact: angle OPT = 90 degrees and angle OQT = 90 degrees. The sum of all four interior angles of a quadrilateral is 360 degrees: angle PTQ + angle OPT + angle OQT + angle POQ = 360 => angle PTQ + 90 + 90 + 110 = 360 => angle PTQ + 290 = 360 => angle PTQ = 360 - 290 = 70 degrees. Thus, angles PTQ and POQ are supplementary.

questions.question: If tangents PA and PB from a point P to a circle with centre O are inclined to each other at an angle of 80 degrees, then what is angle POA?
questions.explanation: Let PA and PB be two tangents drawn from external point P to a circle with center O, inclined to each other at angle APB = 80 degrees. In quadrilateral OAPB, angle OAP = angle OBP = 90 degrees. Because opposite angles are supplementary, angle AOB + angle APB = 180 degrees => angle AOB = 180 - 80 = 100 degrees. The line segment OP connecting the external point to the center bisects the angle subtended by the radii at the center (by RHS triangle congruence). Therefore, angle POA = angle AOB / 2 = 100 / 2 = 50 degrees.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of parallel tangents that a circle can have at any given time?
questions.explanation: A circle can have at most TWO parallel tangents at any given time. Proof: By Theorem 10.1, any tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius drawn through its point of contact. For two tangent lines to be parallel, their corresponding radii must be collinear, meaning they must form a straight line passing through the center of the circle. Since a straight line through the center is a diameter and intersects the circumference at exactly two opposite endpoints, only two parallel tangents can exist across that diameter.

questions.question: The tangents drawn at the endpoints of a diameter of a circle are always:
questions.explanation: Let AB be a diameter of a circle with center O, and let lines l and m be the tangents drawn at endpoints A and B. By Theorem 10.1, the radius OA is perpendicular to tangent line l (angle = 90 degrees), and radius OB is perpendicular to tangent line m (angle = 90 degrees). Diameter AB acts as a transversal intersecting the two straight lines l and m. Because the alternate interior angles are equal (both 90 degrees) and consecutive interior angles sum to 180 degrees, the two tangents are strictly parallel.

questions.question: Two concentric circles are of radii 5 cm and 3 cm. Find the length of the chord of the larger circle which touches the smaller circle.
questions.explanation: Let two concentric circles have center O with radii R = 5 cm and r = 3 cm. Let AB be a chord of the larger circle that touches the smaller inner circle tangentially at point P. By Theorem 10.1, the radius OP of the inner circle is perpendicular to tangent AB. A perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord, so AP = PB. In right-angled triangle OPA: AP = sqrt(OA^2 - OP^2) = sqrt(5^2 - 3^2) = sqrt(25 - 9) = sqrt(16) = 4 cm. Therefore, the total chord length AB = 2 * AP = 2 * 4 = 8 cm.

questions.question: A straight line that intersects a circle at two distinct points is called a:
questions.explanation: In plane geometry, a straight line that intersects a circle at two distinct points is formally defined as a 'Secant'. In contrast, a straight line that touches the circle at exactly one unique point without crossing inside is defined as a 'Tangent', while the line segment bounded between the two points of intersection on the circle is called a 'Chord'. When the two distinct intersection points of a secant move closer and coincide into a single limiting point, the secant line transforms into a tangent line.

questions.subtopic: Number of Tangents from Point on Circle
questions.question: How many tangents can be drawn to a circle passing through a specific point lying ON the circle?
questions.explanation: At any specific, single point lying on the circumference of a circle, exactly ONE unique tangent can be drawn. Proof: By Theorem 10.1, any tangent line touching the circle at point P must be perpendicular to the radius vector OP. In Euclidean plane geometry, through a given point P on a straight line segment OP, there exists one and only one perpendicular straight line. Therefore, only one unique tangent line can be constructed passing through any designated point on the circular circumference.

questions.subtopic: Number of Tangents from Inside Point
questions.question: How many tangents can be drawn to a circle from a point lying strictly inside the circle?
questions.explanation: From a point lying strictly INSIDE the circular boundary of a circle, ZERO (no) tangents can be drawn to the circle. Proof: Any straight line passing through an interior point of a circle must necessarily enter and exit the circular boundary, intersecting the circumference at two distinct points. Consequently, every line passing through an interior point functions as a secant line rather than a tangent line. A tangent line requires that all points on the line except the single point of contact lie outside the circle.

questions.subtopic: Number of Tangents from Outside Point
questions.question: How many tangents can be drawn to a circle from a point lying outside the circle?
questions.explanation: From any point lying strictly outside a circle, exactly TWO distinct tangents can be drawn to touch the circle. Proof: Let P be an external point and O be the center of the circle. By drawing a circle with diameter OP, this secondary circle intersects the original circle at two distinct points, say A and B. Joining PA and PB produces two lines that each subtend a 90-degree angle with radii OA and OB in semi-circles. Thus, lines PA and PB are both tangents, giving exactly two tangents from any external point.

questions.subtopic: Angle Between Tangent and Chord Relation
questions.question: If two tangents TP and TQ are drawn to a circle with centre O from an external point T, then angle PTQ is equal to:
questions.explanation: Let tangents TP and TQ be drawn from external point T to a circle with center O. By Theorem 10.2, TP = TQ, making triangle TPQ isosceles. Therefore, angle TPQ = angle TQP = (180 - angle PTQ) / 2 = 90 - (1/2) * angle PTQ. By Theorem 10.1, radius OP is perpendicular to tangent TP, so angle OPT = 90 degrees. Now, angle OPQ = angle OPT - angle TPQ = 90 - [90 - (1/2) * angle PTQ] = (1/2) * angle PTQ. Multiplying both sides by 2 yields the standard board theorem: angle PTQ = 2 * angle OPQ.

questions.question: PQ is a chord of length 8 cm of a circle of radius 5 cm. The tangents at P and Q intersect at a point T. Find the length of tangent TP.
questions.explanation: Chord PQ has length 8 cm in a circle of radius 5 cm. Tangents at P and Q intersect at T. Line OT is the perpendicular bisector of chord PQ, intersecting PQ at R, so PR = 8/2 = 4 cm. In right-angled triangle OPR: OR = sqrt(OP^2 - PR^2) = sqrt(5^2 - 4^2) = sqrt(25 - 16) = 3 cm. In right-angled triangle OPT, PR is perpendicular to hypotenuse OT. Triangles TRP and PRO are similar (AA criterion): TP / PO = RP / RO => TP / 5 = 4 / 3 => TP = (5 * 4) / 3 = 20/3 cm (approximately 6.67 cm).

questions.explanation: In circle geometry, the unique point where a straight tangent line touches and meets the circumference of the circle is formally designated as the 'point of contact' (or point of tangency). questions.question: A quadrilateral ABCD is drawn to circumscribe a circle. Which of the following relationships is ALWAYS true?
questions.explanation: Let quadrilateral ABCD circumscribe a circle touching at points P (on AB), Q (on BC), R (on CD), and S (on DA). By Theorem 10.2, tangents drawn from each vertex are equal: AP = AS, BP = BQ, CR = CQ, and DR = DS. Adding all four equations: (AP + BP) + (CR + DR) = (AS + DS) + (BQ + CQ). Grouping collinear segment pairs: AP + BP = AB, CR + DR = CD, AS + DS = AD, and BQ + CQ = BC. Substituting these yields the famous identity: AB + CD = AD + BC (sum of opposite sides is equal).

questions.question: If a parallelogram ABCD circumscribes a circle, what special type of quadrilateral must ABCD be?
questions.explanation: If a parallelogram ABCD circumscribes a circle, it must be a Rhombus. Proof: Since ABCD is a circumscribed quadrilateral, the sum of opposite sides is equal: AB + CD = AD + BC. In a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal in length: AB = CD and AD = BC. Substituting these relations into the circumscribing identity: AB + AB = AD + AD => 2*AB = 2*AD => AB = AD. Since adjacent sides of the parallelogram are equal, all four sides must be equal (AB = BC = CD = DA), which proves that ABCD is a rhombus.

questions.question: XY and X'Y' are two parallel tangents to a circle with centre O and another tangent AB with point of contact C intersects XY at A and X'Y' at B. What is the measure of angle AOB?
questions.explanation: Let XY and X'Y' be parallel tangents at endpoints P and Q of diameter PQ. Tangent AB touches the circle at C, intersecting XY at A and X'Y' at B. Triangles OPA and OCA are congruent (RHS), so angle AOP = angle AOC = (1/2)*angle POC. Similarly, triangles OQB and OCB are congruent, so angle BOQ = angle BOC = (1/2)*angle QOC. Since PQ is a straight diameter, angle POC + angle QOC = 180 degrees. Therefore, angle AOB = angle AOC + angle BOC = (1/2)*(angle POC + angle QOC) = (1/2)*180 = 90 degrees.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 10, Exercise 10.2 Question 9

questions.subtopic: Perpendicular to Tangent Passes Through Centre
questions.question: The perpendicular drawn to a tangent at its point of contact passes through:
questions.explanation: By Theorem 10.1, the radius drawn from the center of the circle to the point of contact is strictly perpendicular to the tangent line at that point. In Euclidean geometry, at any given point on a line, there exists only one unique perpendicular straight line in the plane. Because the radius is already perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, any perpendicular line drawn to the tangent at this contact point must be collinear with the radius, and therefore must pass directly through the center of the circle.
